question: About 16 million men share a male-line ancestor who lived in Mongolia about 1,000 years ago. How many doublings turn one man into 16 million?
answer: Four more: 1 million x 16 = 16 million, so 24 doublings in all.
move: Doubling needs far fewer steps than intuition expects.
trap: Guessing hundreds of generations, far more than 1,000 years allow.
hint: The lineage is linked to Genghis Khan's family. Count the doublings to a thousand, then to a million.
steps: Ten doublings turn 1 into 1,024, roughly a thousand.
Ten more turn a thousand into roughly a million.
Four more: 1 million x 16 = 16 million, so 24 doublings in all.
source: Zerjal et al., Am. J. Human Genetics, 2003
reference: Zerjal et al., The Genetic Legacy of the Mongols, American Journal of Human Genetics 72, 2003
